extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates in commutative algebra / algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of completions, a-adic/topological properties, inverse limits, Artin–Rees and Krull intersection results, Hensel lifting, and examples (p-adic, power series, germs). Includes constructions, necessary and sufficient conditions, and counterexamples about exactness, flatness, and integrality after completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness is a local property
rubrics_metrics.description: Exactness of a sequence of modules/maps can be checked locally: if (x1,...,xn) ∈ ker ψ then certain local relations hold and ker ψ ⊆ Im φ; conversely ψ◦φ = 0. Hence the sequence is exact locally and, by Proposition 3.9, exact on the original modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use localization and the given componentwise computations to verify exactness; apply Proposition 3.9 to lift local exactness to global exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of translations and inversion in topological groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiplication (x,y)↦xy is continuous then for fixed a, Ta: y↦ay is continuous (restriction), inversion y↦−y is continuous, and therefore x↦x−y is continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ta and T−a are bijective continuous open maps (Ta(O)=O+a) hence homeomorphisms. To show openness/invariance check images of basic open sets under translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 10.1 — properties of H (intersection of neighborhoods of 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let H = ⋂{neighborhoods of 0} in a topological group G. Then (1) H is a subgroup, (2) H is the closure of {0}, (3) G/H is Hausdorff, (4) G is Hausdorff iff H = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove closure under inversion and addition by intersecting symmetric neighborhoods; show H equals the closure of {0} via neighborhood characterization; use quotient topology to get Hausdorffness and equivalence with H=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of Hausdorff spaces via diagonal
rubrics_metrics.description: X is Hausdorff iff the diagonal D = {(x,x)} ⊂ X×X is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X Hausdorff, for each (x,y)∉D find disjoint open U,V around x,y so U×V avoids D; conversely if D closed then for (x,y)∉D pick product neighborhood U×V disjoint from D to separate x,y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of convergence (sequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: x_v → y means: for every open neighborhood U of y there exists N ∈ N such that for all v > N, x_v ∈ U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard neighborhood definition; used repeatedly for convergence arguments in group and module completions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy equivalence and basic properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Cauchy equivalence of sequences is an equivalence relation. Sum of Cauchy sequences is Cauchy. The image of a Cauchy sequence under a continuous homomorphism is Cauchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove reflexivity/triviality, symmetry by using symmetric neighborhoods, transitivity by choosing V with V+V ⊆ U. For sums use same V argument; for images use preimages of neighborhoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of topology on completion ˆG
rubrics_metrics.description: For open U ⊂ G define ˆU = {ˆx ∈ ˆG : every representing sequence is eventually in U}; these ˆU form a basis for the topology on ˆG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use eventual membership of representatives (Cauchy sequences) to define basic opens; this topology makes canonical map φ:G→ˆG continuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality and continuity of induced maps on completions
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:G→H is a continuous homomorphism then the induced map ˆf:ˆG→ˆH is a continuous homomorphism; φ:G→ˆG is continuous; and ˆ(g◦f)=ˆg◦ˆf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show preimages of basic opens ˆU in ˆH equal ˆ(f^{-1}(U)) in ˆG; check homomorphism property on representatives; use the constant-sequence argument for φ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental system of neighborhoods (neighborhood basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: 0 ∈ G has a fundamental system of neighborhoods if there is a descending sequence G = G0 ⊇ G1 ⊇ ... such that every neighborhood U of 0 contains some Gn. If each Gi is subgroup we call it a fundamental system of neighborhoods consisting of subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a sequence yields neighborhood bases at all points via translates g+Gn; used to build group topologies (e.g., p-adic topology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topology generated by neighborhood basis of subgroups: Gn open and closed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the basis is cosets g+Gn for all g and n, then each Gn is both open and closed in the generated topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gn is open because it's a basis element; closed because it's a union of cosets disjoint from its complement (or complement is union of other basis elements). This property supports finite-index/compactness arguments (typical example: p-adic topology).

rubrics_metrics.name: A group with the coset basis is a topological group
rubrics_metrics.description: With basis g+Gn the group operations are continuous: addition µ(x,y)=x+y and inversion x↦−x are continuous, and translations are continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neighborhood definition: for x+y+Gn find (x+Gn)×(y+Gn) mapping inside it; for inversion use −Gn=Gn since Gn subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: a-adic topology makes A a topological ring
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ideals {a^n} as a fundamental system at 0, the topology whose basis is cosets g+a^n makes A a topological ring: addition and multiplication are continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show multiplication continuity: for neighborhood xy + a^n pick (x+a^n)×(y+a^n) and use expansion xy + x a^n + y a^n + a^{2n} ⊆ xy + a^n; rely on ideal properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion commutes with finite direct sums and split exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion (ˆ·) preserves finite direct sums; completion applied to a split exact sequence gives split exactness on completions (Corollary 10.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of direct sum as split exact sequence; apply Proposition 10.2 about inverse limits and exactness to conclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion preserves exactness under Noetherian/finiteness hypotheses (Proposition 10.13 / 10.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Noetherian hypotheses (finite generation), completion maps (and induced maps like α, β, γ, δ in diagrams) are surjective or injective as required so exact sequences remain exact after completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use finite generation to apply Lemma 10.8 twice (to get finite generation of duals) and Artin–Rees stability with Proposition 10.12 to lift exactness to completions; diagram chasing yields injectivity of α, surjectivity of other maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units in the completion and Jacobson radical containment (Prop.10.15 iv)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ξ_n = 1 + x + ... + x^n in ˆA the sequence is Cauchy and converges in ˆA; for x∈ˆa, 1−x is a unit in ˆA. Hence ˆa ⊆ Jacobson_radical(ˆA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometric series argument in the complete ring: (1−x)·lim ξ_n = 1. Conclude Nakayama-style facts about ˆa acting nilpotently on finitely generated modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull intersection theorem (Theorem 10.17) via Artin–Rees
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Artin–Rees lemma one gets that ⋂_{n≥0} a^n M equals certain stable intersection and aE = E implies E equals M∩(⋂ a^n M) etc, hence Krull's intersection conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Artin–Rees to show filtration stabilizes and derive bounded differences so topologies coincide; deduce intersection statements and equality results on modules annihilated by powers of a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated graded ring G(A) and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: G(A) (the associated graded ring relative to a) has well-defined multiplication modulo a^{m+n+1} and, if a is generated by s elements, G(A) ≅ (A/a)[x_1,...,x_s] as a ring (grading identifies monomials giving generators of a^k/a^{k+1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check multiplicative relations using representative lifts and verify bijectivity and multiplicative homomorphism using degree-by-degree arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of inverse limits and exactness (Lemma 10.23, Prop 10.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inverse limits are left-exact but not necessarily right-exact; the inverse limit functor preserves injectivity under certain surjectivity hypotheses on transition maps (use of five-lemma style diagram chasing), and lim^1 measures failure of exactness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the inverse system maps are surjective (Mittag-Leffler condition) one gets exactness of limits; use Proposition 10.2 and diagram chasing to deduce injectivity/surjectivity of induced maps on limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion (inverse limit) is not right exact in general — explicit p-adic counterexample
rubrics_metrics.description: There are exact sequences 0→A→B→B→0 (multiplication-by-p) whose completions ˆA→ˆB→ˆB→0 are not exact; explicit computations with A = ⊕_{n≥0} Z/p^nZ, B = ... show ker(ˆp·−) ≠ image(ˆα). lim^1 terms can be nonzero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute inverse systems A/(p^kA) and B/(p^kB) explicitly, identify ˆB ≅ ∏ Z/p^nZ and find coherent sequences and kernels; use Snake lemma and lim^1 computations to see failure of right exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of ˆM = 0 via support and Nakayama lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: ˆM = 0 iff ˆM = ˆa·ˆM (Nakayama) iff M = E (module annihilated by 1 + a), and this is equivalent to Supp(M) ∩ V(a) = ∅ (maximal ideals containing a are not in Supp(M)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Nakayama on completions, Krull intersection, and localization arguments: if p ⊇ a then Ep=0 so p∉Supp(M); conversely absence from V(a) implies vanishing intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness preserves injectivity of multiplication by non-zero-divisors
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is not a zero divisor on A, then 0→A -×x→ A is exact; if ˆA is flat over A then 0→ˆA -×x→ ˆA is exact, so x remains non-zero-divisor after flat completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply flatness (exactness of tensoring with ˆA) to preserve injectivity of multiplication maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion can destroy integrality — explicit counterexample
rubrics_metrics.description: An integral domain A (e.g., k[x,y]/(y^2−x^2−x^3)) may have completion ˆA that is not a domain because the defining polynomial becomes reducible in k[[x,y]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show existence of formal power series f with f^2 = 1 + x so y^2 − x^2 − x^3 factors as (y + x f)(y − x f) in the complete ring, using power series expansion for sqrt(1+x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completions and localization compatibility: (M_a)_b = M_{a+b} and related isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For finitely generated modules M, localization and completion satisfy compatibilities: M_a ≅ A_a ⊗_A M and (M_a)_b ≅ M_{a+b}; completions over equivalent filtrations give same topology and same completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare inverse systems A/(a_n + b_m) and show the induced topologies coincide; use exact sequences and Prop.10.12 to propagate completions across quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hensel lifting (constructive factor lifting by inverse limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a factorization of f mod m with coprime monic factors, one can inductively construct coprime monic polynomials g_k,h_k with degrees r,n−r such that f−g_k h_k ∈ m^k, with g_{k+1}≡g_k mod m^k; completeness of A yields limiting g,h with f=gh in A[x].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Bezout in (A/m)[x] to write xp = a_p g_{k−1} + b_p h_{k−1} up to m, control degrees of a_p,b_p, form corrections g_k=g_{k−1}+Σ c_p b_p, h_k=h_{k−1}+Σ c_p a_p, and take limits componentwise (Cauchy) in the complete ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hensel lemma applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If f has a simple root α in A/m, Hensel lemma lifts to a root a ∈ A congruent to α; gives construction of 7-adic square roots (e.g., 3 lifts to √2 in Z_7) and solves parametrized equations over k[[x]] producing formal power series solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify derivative/non-degeneracy hypotheses (simple root) modulo m and apply lifting; for power series use A=k[[x]] with m=(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Units in power-series-type ring B: nonzero constant term implies invertibility (Claim LVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f∈B (ring of germs/power-series-like functions) has nonzero constant term then f is a unit in B (use geometric series inversion); B is local with maximal ideal m=(z1,...,zn), and A⊂B⊂ˆA with completions equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize constant term to 1, invert via geometric series (1−g)^{-1}=Σ g^k; check convergence/radius for analytic-type B; deduce locality and flatness relations A→B→ˆA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring of germs of C^∞ functions at 0: structure and completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be germs of C^∞ functions at 0. The maximal ideal m consists of germs vanishing at 0; m^k = {[f] : f^{(j)}(0)=0 for j<k} = ([x^k]); A/m^k ≅ R[x]/(x^k); completion ˆA ≅ R[[x]] (Taylor series). A is not Noetherian though ˆA is Noetherian and finitely generated as an A-module; the map A→ˆA is surjective by Borel's theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Taylor theorem to identify representatives modulo m^k and pass to inverse limit to get formal power series; show existence of non-Noetherian behavior in A (e.g., nonzero flat function with all derivatives 0).
